api.rationale: Identifies the API proxy, and the correct value is organisation-specific.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the deployment can be accidentally deleted or removed from Terraform management.

environment.rationale: Identifies the deployment environment, and the correct value is organisation-specific.

org_id.rationale: Identifies the Apigee organisation and does not directly configure a security control.

override.description: If true, replaces other deployed revisions of this proxy in the environment.
override.rationale: Controls the functional deployment behaviour for replacing an existing API proxy revision. It does not directly configure access, data protection, encryption, exposure, or another security control, making it unsuitable as a generic platform-level security policy target.

revision.description: API proxy revision number to deploy.
revision.rationale: Identifies the proxy revision, and there is no universally secure revision number.

sequenced_rollout.description: If true, enables sequenced rollout for safe traffic switching.
sequenced_rollout.rationale: Controls the deployment strategy used to switch traffic between API proxy revisions. Although it may improve service availability during deployment, it is an operational rollout setting rather than a security control or destructive-loss safeguard.

service_account.description: Optional service account the deployed proxy runs as.
service_account.rationale: Determines the workload identity and permissions used by the deployed API proxy at runtime. Enforcing an appropriate, dedicated service account supports least-privilege access and reduces the risk of the proxy receiving excessive permissions or accessing unauthorised resources.
